title: Return value of left-sequencing
statement: A value of type $\mathrm{TimeM}\,T\,\alpha$ is a computation carrying both a return value in $\alpha$ and an accumulated cost in $T$; write $\mathrm{ret}$ for the return-value component. Suppose $T$ is equipped with an addition, let $x$ be such a computation of type $\mathrm{TimeM}\,T\,\alpha$, and let $y$ be a (thunked) computation of type $\mathrm{TimeM}\,T\,\beta$. Then the left-sequencing $x \mathbin{<{*}} y$, which runs both computations and adds their costs but keeps only the value produced by $x$, has return value $\mathrm{ret}(x \mathbin{<{*}} y) = \mathrm{ret}(x)$.
hypotheses_covered: x is a computation of type TimeM T α
y is a (thunked) computation of type TimeM T β
